Creative Performing Arts
Head of Creative Performing Arts Faculty:Amy Percival apercival@bohuntwokingham.com
Creative Performing Arts
Intent
Our faculty is committed to nurturing the holistic development of our students, guiding them on a journey of self-discovery and self-worth through Physical Education (PE) and the Arts. Our curriculum provides diverse opportunities for each student to unlock their full potential as individuals.
Here is how we achieve this…
Holistic Development: We recognise the importance of fostering not just academic excellence but also personal growth. Our curriculum integrates elements of PE and the Arts to offer a well-rounded educational experience that nurtures physical, emotional, and creative dimensions of our students.
Collaborative Learning: Through collaborative projects and interdisciplinary connections, students are encouraged to work together, explore diverse perspectives, and delve deeper into their understanding of themselves and the world around them. By looking beyond the obvious, they uncover layers of their identity and potential.
Self-Exploration and Risk-Taking: We empower students to embrace self-discovery by providing a supportive environment where they feel encouraged to take risks and explore new territories. Whether it’s through physical challenges in PE or creative expression in the Arts, students learn to push boundaries, expand their comfort zones, and discover hidden talents.
Cultural Capital: Our curriculum is enriched with opportunities for students to engage with diverse cultural experiences and heritage through PE and the Arts. By immersing themselves in different cultural contexts, students develop a broader perspective, appreciation, and respect for diversity, thus enriching their cultural capital.
Confidence and Well-Roundedness: Through their journey with us, students not only develop competence in PE and artistic skills but also cultivate qualities of confidence, resilience, and adaptability. They leave Bohunt Wokingham as well-rounded individuals, equipped with the skills, knowledge, and self-assurance to thrive in a dynamic and interconnected world.
In essence, our intent is to inspire and empower students to explore their identities, embrace challenges, and cultivate a lifelong appreciation for Physical Education and the Arts, laying the foundation for their continued growth and success beyond their time at our school.

Tickets Now on Sale for the School Production of Matilda Jr!
The team that brought you ‘Grease School Edition’ and ‘Little Shop of Horrors’, are thrilled to invite you to experience our exciting school production of Matilda Jr., running from June 30th to July 2nd! Doors open at 6:45 PM, with the show starting promptly at 7 PM.
Seats are available on a first-come, first-served basis, so make sure to arrive early. Please note that there will not be an interval and the play runs for approximately 60 mins. Additionally, the show includes strobe and flashing lighting effects, so please keep this in mind when booking your tickets.
Inspired by the beloved book by Roald Dahl, Matilda Jr. is a hilarious, heart-warming and high-energy musical packed with unforgettable songs and larger-than-life characters.
Matilda is a bright and imaginative young girl with a love of books and a mind of her own. Despite being misunderstood by her parents and terrorised by the fearsome Miss Trunchbull at school, Matilda discovers she has the courage to change her story. Alongside her kind teacher Miss Honey and her friends, she proves that even the smallest person can make a big difference.
Filled with humour, rebellion and heart, this spectacular production is perfect for audiences of all ages.
Don’t miss your chance to enjoy this unforgettable night of music, laughter and inspiring performances as our talented cast brings this magical story to life on stage!
Tickets are available from TicketSource. Please follow the links for the performance days: 30th June 1st July 2nd July
For more details, please contact Mrs Percival at apercival@bohuntwokingham.com.

* All jewellery must be removed before students take part in a PE lesson, TAPING of earrings is NOT permitted
* White Sport Socks will be permitted in the Summer Term (Post Easter) for Athletics, Cricket and Rounders.
* Hair tied up for all lessons
The PE department holds the very highest of standards for students during lessons and whilst representing the school in Sport. We ask that students arrive for all lessons ready to learn and with the correct equipment. If a student does not have the correct equipment then the teachers will sanction through our centralised detention system:
If you cannot take part in the lesson, i.e. you cannot remove jewellery or you do not bring the correct footwear, this carries a sanction of a one hour centralised detention as the student has missed out on learning.
If you can take part however have incorrect items, i.e. you are wearing the wrong socks, this carries a sanction of a 30 minute centralised detention as the student has not had correct equipment, however learning has not been lost.
If your kit is incorrect for a reason out of your control, please bring a note to explain the different kit (but this needs to be all black)
Co-curricular Activity:
Co-curricular kit has the same expectations as the kit expectation in lessons.
If a student is ill / injured and is therefore unable to take part in a practical PE lesson, parents / guardians should send a dated and signed note for the attention of the PE department.
If the illness / injury is considered long term / ongoing the parents / guardians should provide a doctor’s note to advise PE staff of this.
In the event that a student is unable to take part in a PE lesson the student must still bring their PE kit. Injured and ill students will still change into full kit. The only exception will be when students are unable to physically change due to the injury impairing their ability to do so without assistance. (For example a fractured arm resulting in a cast).
Throughout the academic year Bohunt School Wokingham will be competing in a number of competitions across a range of sports. These competitions include (but are not limited to):
Athletics: The RSAA Competition (Palmer Park), The Wokingham Athletics Championships. Wokingham Sports hall athletics, The ESAA Track and Field Championships.
Cricket: The Berkshire League
Basketball: The Berkshire League
Football (Boys): The RSFA League, The EBSFA League, The ESFA Cup, The Berkshire County Cup, The Reading 5-aside Tournament, Friendly Fixtures.
Football (Girls): The RSFA League, The EBSFA League, The ESFA Cup, The Berkshire County Cup, The Reading 5-aside Tournament, The Swift 5-a-side Tournament, Friendly Fixtures.
Handball: The Berkshire League
Netball: The Wokingham schools league, The Sisters in Sport National Cup, Friendly Fixtures.
Rugby (Boys): TheRSFA League, The Berkshire Festival of Rugby, The Reading Abbey Invitational, The Reading RFC 7s Tournament, Friendly Fixtures, Roslyn Park 7’s.
Rugby Girls (Girls): The RSFA League, Friendly Fixtures, The Reading Abbey Invitational, RP7’s.
For students to be selected to compete for the school teams they should attend training regularly, meet PE department expectations during lessons and extra-curricular activity and meet Bohunt School expectations during other lessons. Students in detention on the date of a fixture will not be selected to play. If a student is on report or an IBP (following suspension) they will be ineligible for selection for the duration of that report/IBP.
Parents are always welcome to come and watch the fixtures that start after school hours.
All fixtures information can be found at www.bohuntwokinghamsport.com
This includes fixtures, results, team sheets, match reports and league standings. Team Sheets can be accessed using the following password: Bohunt25
In addition, the PE department has a twitter account, this will feature news, fixtures, results, team sheets and photographs. Follow us at: @BohuntSport
Any other questions please do not hesitate to contact the PE department.

Careers and Guidance
Bohunt School Wokingham is committed to providing students with high quality information, advice and guidance regarding education pathways, apprenticeships and careers.
We aim to help students make informed decisions at key times in their education, for example with option choices in Year 8, post 16 plans in Year 11 as they plan for university or working life. In addition to dedicated careers input for all year groups, the school’s programme includes interaction with universities and the local business community.
We support our students in making well-informed decisions by providing access to differentiated, impartial and independent information and guidance about the range of options (including academic, vocational, apprenticeships) that are most likely to help them to achieve their ambitions. We believe that giving students the best careers education and guidance is vital to improving their motivation to learn and help them to achieve.
All students will be entitled to a careers education, information, advice and guidance programme that:
Careers Lead: Miss Wendy Sales
Email: wsales@bohuntwokingham.com
Here is the Spring Term 2026 Inspiring Opportunities Newsletter from Innervate for you to explore.
Inside, you’ll find the latest updates on apprenticeships, work experience opportunities and careers events taking place over the coming months, alongside useful resources to support decision-making about next steps after school or college. We also explore the impact of artificial intelligence on the future job landscape.

Geography Department
Intent
Geography is a relevant and exciting subject to study today. Many of the world’s current problems are deeply linked to geography and need future geographers to help solve them.
Here at Bohunt Wokingham we develop geographers who:
To facilitate the development of geographers we aim to provide a rich and diverse curriculum where students can study a wide range of human and physical issues. Students can expect to learn about relevant examples from around the world on current issues like climate change, migration and resource shortages. We aim to provide a range of enrichment opportunities including fieldwork trips, both locally and internationally. Through studying the subject, we hope students develop a love and understanding of the world around them.
